assumptions: Hosts keep exporting OTLP HTTP/JSON and posting hooks as documented on 2026-10-31 (unverified until host verification); empty-bodied HTTP hook responses are non-blocking (unverified until T030); the Claude desktop browser pane loads loopback pages (unverified until T032); the viewer runs on the same machine as the hosts; ADR 0032 and ADR 0033 are decided before implementation.
compatibility: New contract agent-braid-loom/v0.1, new effort pack contract agent-braid-loom-effort-pack/v0.1, new surfaces matrix agent-braid-view-surfaces/v0.1 and new optional command group agent-braid view. No change to existing contracts, the plugin package, the portable MCP surface, the SPEC-047 telemetry store or frozen evidence. Vendored Three.js adds an MIT directory under ADR 0033.
domain: Local machine, loopback interface, Agent Braid artifacts of the current contracts (analysis, Git replay plan, scheduler preparations, runtime grants and state, SPEC-057 ownership outputs as JSON, SPEC-052 gate phases and results, allowlisted usage fields of host stream events) and Claude Code and Codex telemetry shapes recorded in fixtures. Not covered: transcripts, Codex hooks and notify, cloud sessions, IDE extensions, other hosts.
execution_contract: Read-only. No route, command or control executes, schedules, grants, retries, cancels or writes to repositories, registries, run directories or host configuration; executionAuthorization is the constant false; hook routes accept only observational events and answer with empty bodies, so the viewer takes no part in host decisions; network use is limited to a loopback server with separate read and ingest credentials; effort data stays in memory; files are written only to an explicit --record file (effort only with --record-effort) and explicit export destinations, created exclusively with owner-only permissions.
hypotheses: None. Q-VIS1 is an open question, not a hypothesis: does seeing the braid shorten the time an operator needs to locate a hazard or conflicting pair compared with reading the JSON receipt? It has no falsification condition, supports no claim and is not a requirement; an optional owner-run descriptive observation may be recorded, and null or inconclusive results are valid.
observation_contract: Owned fixtures and recorded host payloads; byte comparison of adapter outputs against source artifacts; HTTP requests against a loopback test server; file-system snapshots for persistence checks; host behavior only through owner-run receipts recorded separately with environment and limits.

scenarios.given: the schema and a corpus of valid and seeded invalid events
scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure_001 record: command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits.
scenarios.then: valid lines pass and every line with an unknown kind, a missing or non-false `executionAuthorization`, a crossing without an integer class, a gate result with a class other than 0, an effort event with a class, a status, action or phase outside its source enum, free text with a control or bidirectional-override character, an `evidenceRef` path that is absolute, has a drive prefix or contains `..`, `notAGuarantee` false, a non-increasing `seq`, duplicate JSON members, a non-finite number or an oversized line is refused with a stable reason and no partial acceptance.

requirements.text: Versioned event contract: Every event is one JSON object per line with `schemaVersion` `agent-braid-loom/v0.1`, a strictly increasing integer `seq`, a `kind` from a closed list, a relative monotonic time `at` (`relMs`, `basis`), a `source` (`adapter`, `evidenceRef`, `host`, `verification`), an `assurance` block (`compatibilityClass`, `notAGuarantee: true`) and `executionAuthorization` fixed to `false`. `compatibilityClass` is the Article 13 class declared by the per-pair analysis fact a crossing carries, `0` for workflow-gate results (their source declares `0-heuristic`) and `null` for every other kind. `verification` (`rehashed`, `unverified`, `derived`) is assigned by the viewer when it ingests an event and is never trusted from a file or a post. Free-text fields reject C0 and C1 control characters, DEL and bidirectional overrides. Source identifiers such as `sha256:` analysis and plan digests are carried verbatim. The closed kinds are `session.origin`, `analysis.report`, `strand.open`, `strand.update`, `strand.close`, `crossing.classified`, `wave.planned`, `wave.started`, `wave.finished`, `grant.issued`, `grant.consumed`, `grant.expired`, `grant.refused`, `hazard.noticed`, `gate.phase`, `gate.result`, `runtime.phase`, `effort.sample` and `observation.gap`. Status, mode, action and phase values are copied verbatim from their source contracts (for example the six Git runtime phases). Lines are at most 16 KiB. A file with more than 50 000 events is refused; the live in-memory ring instead evicts old events and announces each evicted range (REQ-006). The schema and an illustrative example are in [contracts/](contracts/).

scenarios.given: the owned fixtures for each artifact family
scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure_002 record: command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits.
scenarios.then: both outputs are byte-identical, every crossing equals one pair of the source analysis with the same classification, shared resources, evidence block and class, every oversized pair is replaced by a `stream-truncated` gap, every status, action and phase equals its source value, every hazard keeps all its units, host stream messages, prompts and tool data are absent, every event's `evidenceRef` hash matches the artifact, and a static import check finds no ownership import in any viewer module.

requirements.text: Artifact adapters bound to evidence: Deterministic adapters translate, without recomputing or reinterpreting them: analysis reports (report-level summary, uncertainty and limits; per pair the classification, shared resources, reasons, constraints, evidence method, coverage, rule set and compatibility class), Git replay plans, scheduler preparations (waves and workers), runtime grants and phases, ownership pre-flight notices and receipts read as JSON files, workflow-gate phases and results (gate pairs carry no per-pair evidence block and are not drawn as crossings) and host stream events (`claude -p` stream-json, `codex exec --json`) through a field allowlist that keeps only usage counts, model and identifiers. Each event carries an `evidenceRef` (artifact path relative to its declared root, plus a SHA-256 of the artifact bytes) and `verification: rehashed`. Events the viewer derives rather than reads (a grant expiry observed after its recorded validity) carry `derived: true` and `verification: derived`. Each adapter lists the source schema versions it supports; another version yields a `source-unsupported` gap instead of a guess. Grants keep the source `action`; hazards keep every unit they name; runtime phases keep the `manifestDigest`; scheduler waves keep the `scheduleDigest` and are joined to a Git plan only where an artifact records the join. A pair whose shared resources, reasons or constraints exceed the per-field caps is not emitted; a `stream-truncated` gap names its report instead. Viewer modules do not import `agent_braid.ownership` and contain no ownership command name.

scenarios.then: each is refused with its contract status and no state change, every hook response body is empty, no access log line is written, the socket is bound to a loopback address only, and every route is read-only or an ingest route that only appends events to memory.

requirements.text: Loopback server boundary: `agent-braid view serve` binds only to `127.0.0.1` (or `::1`) and uses two per-session credentials with separate rights: a one-time open code, printed at start, that the browser exchanges once for an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict` session cookie granting read routes only; and an ingest token, written to a new owner-only file and sent by host exporters as an `Authorization: Bearer` header, granting ingest routes only. No credential remains in a URL after the exchange, in an access log or in printed host configuration. Requests with a `Host` other than the bound loopback names, a foreign `Origin`, a cross-site `Sec-Fetch-Site`, a missing or wrong credential, an oversized body, a missing `Content-Length`, a content encoding other than identity, a wrong content type, duplicate JSON members or non-finite numbers are refused with the statuses in the [UI, security and privacy contract](contracts/ui-security-privacy.md#refusal-statuses). Responses carry the contract's Content Security Policy with no remote origins. Every response to a hook route has an empty body. The server exposes no route that executes, schedules, grants, writes to a repository or changes host configuration. Limits: 256 strands, 4 096 crossings, 64 waves, 1 024 grants, 8 concurrent subscribers, 32 concurrent connections and a 10-second socket timeout; OTLP bodies at most 1 MiB and hook bodies at most 256 KiB. Input beyond a per-kind cap (for example a report with more than 4 096 pairs) is not stored and is announced by a `stream-truncated` gap.

scenarios.given: recorded payload fixtures for each host shape, including payloads carrying prompt text, tool output and unknown attributes
scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure_005 record: command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits.
scenarios.then: only allowlisted attributes keep values in events, decision hook events are refused with an empty body, log bodies are absent, no dropped value is present in the store, in any response or in any export, unknown attribute names appear only in the names inventory, identifiers differ between two server sessions, and unknown shapes produce a `shape-unpinned` gap.

requirements.text: Live host ingest with an attribute allowlist: The server accepts OTLP HTTP/JSON logs and metrics (Claude Code `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY` export; Codex `[otel]` export) and Claude Code HTTP hook payloads for observational events only (`SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, `PostToolUse`). Decision events such as `PreToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `UserPromptSubmit` and `Stop` are refused, and the viewer never takes part in a host decision. Codex `notify` and command hooks need a local shim and belong to VIS.3. Only the attributes of the canonical allowlist in the [UI, security and privacy contract](contracts/ui-security-privacy.md#data-minimization) keep their values, at every OTLP level (resource, scope, record and data point); log bodies are dropped and only the event name is kept; kept values are length-bounded and follow the free-text rule. Identifiers are replaced by values salted per server session. Prompt text, message text, tool input, tool output and file content are dropped before storage. The names (never values) of dropped attributes are kept in a bounded in-memory inventory for host verification. An unrecognized shape yields `observation.gap` `shape-unpinned` instead of a guess.

requirements.text: Replay and live delivery: The same viewer consumes a recorded loom file (`--replay`) and the live store. Server-Sent Events resume from `Last-Event-ID`; evicted events are announced by a `ring-evicted` gap; `/snapshot` returns the current state. Artifact directories named with `--watch` are polled with fixed bounds: at most 8 roots, 4 096 files, 16 MiB read per file, known artifact names only, regular files opened without following symbolic links and resolving inside their root, every 500 ms. Replayed events and adapter events whose artifact cannot be re-hashed are marked `unverified` and rendered with a distinct unverified marker.

requirements.text: Ephemeral effort and explicit recording: Effort data (tokens, cost, durations) lives in process memory, is labeled `basis: host-estimate`, uses relative monotonic time and is never written to the SPEC-047 telemetry store or to a repository. `serve` writes nothing unless the user passes `--record FILE`, which writes the loom stream to a new private file outside repositories (destination rules of REQ-008); effort events are recorded only with the additional flag `--record-effort`. A recording holds at most 49 999 events followed by one `stream-truncated` gap, so every recording stays replayable and exportable. Recording files are created exclusively, without following a symbolic link, with owner-only permissions.

By default it omits `effort.sample` events and replaces absolute-path-like values in every string field with a fixed marker. Output is deterministic for the same input.

requirements.text: Comparative effort evidence pack: With `--include-effort`, a `--baseline NAME` and two or more `--arm NAME=FILE` recordings made with `--record-effort`, each with an `--arm-note NAME=TEXT` selection note, export adds effort totals per arm, strand, host and model, a summary and a static HTML/SVG rendering without scripts or remote resources. Arm names match `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}`. All text in HTML, SVG and Markdown outputs is escaped, `index.html` carries a restrictive meta Content Security Policy, and `summary.md` contains no link or image syntax. The non-claim statement and the `host-estimate` label appear in `index.html` and in every SVG chart as well as in `summary.md` and `manifest.json`. Comparisons are pairwise between the baseline arm and each other arm. The pack records how each arm was selected and states that arms are unmatched unless the owner records a matching. Each comparison uses the shape of `agent-braid harness compare`: a `differences` list of `{field, left, right}` rows, where a field absent from one arm appears as `null` on that side and never as zero, and comparison-level `identical` and `unlistedChange`. Every figure is labeled `host-estimate` and `empirical` and carries no compatibility class; the pack states that it is not a speedup, saving or causal claim. Registering the pack as a Braid Harness record kind is a HAR decision outside VIS.1. The contract is in [contracts/effort-evidence-pack.md](contracts/effort-evidence-pack.md).

requirements.text: Web viewer bound to facts: The viewer renders strands, crossings, waves, grants, gates, hazards, effort and gaps following the visual grammar in [research.md](research.md#visual-grammar). Every visible element maps to one event; selecting it shows the event, its compatibility class as a categorical label, shared resources, evidence method, coverage, reasons, constraints, the report's uncertainty and limits, the `evidenceRef` and its verification status. Unverified crossings and gate results carry a distinct unverified marker. Only `independent-candidate` pairs are drawn as strand swaps; ordered, conflicting and unknown pairs have their own glyphs and never look like a clean swap; strands that pass between non-adjacent lanes are drawn as visibly uncrossed bridges. Classes are shown categorically, never as a safety ordering, and the legend states that a class is not a guarantee. Counters show only measures the events support: conflicts flagged, ordered pairs, independent candidates, unknown pairs, planned wave width shown alone and labeled "advisory plan, not a runtime measurement", hazards, gaps, gates and grants. No counter shows speedup or a ratio against serial execution. Lane ordering is a layout choice and never a braid simplification. Three.js is vendored at a pinned version with a hash manifest; first-party files reference no remote origin and the bundle performs no remote load. If ADR 0033 is not accepted, the table view and SVG frames are the VIS.1 surface. A text table view of the same model is available without WebGL.

scientific_limits: Engineering specification. Claim level inspiration (Article 17): the braid picture is a structural analogy (Article 18) used as a representation of computed classifications, not a braid-theoretic result; no braid relation or simplification is applied, and a drawn swap or wave is not permission to interleave (Article 6). Replayed and host-reported events are unverified. Effort figures are empirical host estimates without a compatibility class, and support no speedup, cost-saving or causal claim. Q-VIS1 is an open question; an optional owner-run observation would be small, unblinded and descriptive. The viewer holds several never-collect categories outside telemetry, listed as deviations for owner review. Structural checks are not owner approval.

Specification only; VIS.2-VIS.4 are derived tracks.
